source: The pre-release review of 8.0.0-beta.9 (finding C-5), decided by the coordinator on 2026-11-25; RFC 7515 §4.1.11; RFC 0014 R1
statement: A token is read whole or not at all: CoSec's verifier reads the JWS crit header of every token it verifies, access and refresh, on every path (the pipeline, refresh, switch, logout), once the signature is verified. This version understands no critical header parameter, so a token whose protected header names any in a well-formed crit is refused, never read without it: TokenNotUnderstoodException, which the pipeline and the served login routes answer 503 unavailable, a refusal a client must not take for the end of its session. A malformed crit (not a non-empty array of distinct names, a name the header does not hold, or a header parameter the JOSE specifications register) is an invalid token, 401 token-invalid. A header member no crit names is ignored. Only a verification that succeeded is cached, so no cache hit answers for a token with crit. A TokenVerifier of an application refuses what its crit names and it does not understand.
guards: jwt:TokenCritTest#a token whose crit names an extension is not read, whichever path verifies it - IDN-47
jwt:TokenCritTest#a malformed crit is an invalid token - IDN-47
jwt:TokenCritTest#a token without crit reads as before, and a header member it does not mark critical is ignored - IDN-47
jwt:TokenCritTest#the cache never answers for a token with crit - IDN-47
jwt:TokenCritTest#the served refresh and logout routes answer a token with crit 503, and a malformed crit 401 - IDN-47
